title: UK 13 A plug fuse replacement
diagnosis: A blown cartridge fuse is the most common reason a plug suddenly goes dead. We'll unplug it, open the cover, swap in a new fuse of the right rating and check the wiring before closing it up.
tools_needed: Replacement BS 1362 cartridge fuse (3 A or 13 A to suit the appliance)
Small flat screwdriver or thin blade (optional, for levering the fuse)
safety_notes: Switch off at the wall and pull the plug out of the socket before touching anything. Never open a plug that is in a socket.
Only use a proper BS 1362 cartridge fuse of the right rating: never foil, wire or a nail.
If you see scorching, melting, cracks or damaged cable inside, stop: do not use the plug and replace it or call an electrician.

steps.title: Make it safe
steps.instruction: Switch off at the wall socket, then pull the plug fully out of the socket. Put it on a table with the back cover facing up.
steps.expected_visual_state: The plug is lying on a table, completely out of any socket, back cover facing the camera.
common_mistakes: Opening the plug while it is still in the socket
Pulling on the cable instead of the plug body to unplug it

steps.title: Undo the cover screw
steps.instruction: Unscrew the single central cover screw with a cross-head screwdriver. Keep the screw somewhere it can't roll away.
steps.expected_visual_state: The cover screw is removed and sitting on the table beside the plug.
common_mistakes: Using a screwdriver that is too small and rounding the screw head

steps.title: Lift off the cover
steps.instruction: Lift the back cover straight off to expose the terminals and fuse. Look inside for any burn marks or damage.
steps.expected_visual_state: The cover is off and the tray is open, showing the three terminals, the cord grip and the fuse in its clips.
common_mistakes: Forcing the cover sideways instead of lifting it
Ignoring scorch marks or melted plastic inside, which means stop and replace the plug

steps.title: Remove the blown fuse
steps.instruction: Gently lever the cartridge fuse out of its clips using a small flat screwdriver or your fingernail. Check it against the replacement.
steps.expected_visual_state: The old fuse is out of the clips and held or lying beside the plug, with the empty fuse clips visible.
common_mistakes: Bending the brass fuse clips by prying too hard
Levering against the live wire or terminal

steps.title: Fit the new fuse
steps.instruction: Choose a fuse of the right rating: 3 A for lamps, chargers and TVs, 13 A for heaters and kettles. Press it firmly into the clips until it snaps in.
steps.expected_visual_state: A new cartridge fuse sits level and snug in both fuse clips, with its rating printed on the end visible.
common_mistakes: Fitting a higher rating than the appliance needs
Not pushing the fuse fully into both clips
Using foil or wire instead of a proper fuse

steps.title: Check wires and cord grip
steps.instruction: Check brown is at live, blue at neutral and green-and-yellow at earth, with no loose strands or bare copper outside the terminals. Make sure the cord grip clamps the grey outer sheath and its screws are tight.
steps.expected_visual_state: Each wire sits under its own terminal screw, no bare copper is visible outside the terminals, and the cord grip is clamped over the grey cable sheath.
common_mistakes: Cord grip clamping the coloured wires instead of the outer sheath
Leaving stray copper strands touching another terminal

steps.title: Close up and test
steps.instruction: Put the cover back on and tighten the cover screw. Only then plug it into the socket, switch on and check the appliance works.
steps.expected_visual_state: The cover is on and flush with the body, the screw is tight, and the appliance powers on when plugged in.
common_mistakes: Plugging in before the cover is screwed on
Overtightening the screw and cracking the cover
Pinching the cable under the cover edge
